selected_evidence.requirement: inventory-maintenance script exists, is executable, and runs correctly
selected_evidence.summary: Discovered the script was corrupted (leftover heredoc text), rewrote it as valid POSIX sh, chmod 0755, and confirmed it runs producing the expected output.

selected_evidence.requirement: Cron job scheduled daily at 02:15 running the script and appending to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
selected_evidence.summary: Installed root crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' and manually executed the exact cron command line, confirming the log file is created and contains the expected line.
Captured boot_id=5fb1b173..., uptime -s, crond active, crontab entry present, and existing log contents before restart.
Issued 'systemctl reboot' via a backgrounded/disowned shell so the exec call acknowledged and returned immediately, before the node disconnected.

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof the node actually restarted (changed boot identity)
selected_evidence.summary: First poll still showed old boot_id (reboot not yet executed), second poll hit connection reset (node rebooting), third poll showed boot_id changed to ac5fb70b... and a later uptime -s, proving the restart occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron service, job, script, and log data
selected_evidence.summary: After reconnect, confirmed crond active/enabled, crontab entry intact, script still executable, prior log content preserved, and a fresh script run successfully appended a new log line.
